name: North Saanich

facts.text: North Saanich adopted Tree Protection Bylaw No. 1548 on October 3, 2022, replacing Bylaw No. 935. Removing any tree it regulates needs a permit.
facts.sourceTitle: Tree Protection | District of North Saanich
facts.excerpt: A tree permit is required to remove any trees regulated by the District's Tree Protection Bylaw No. 1548.
facts.note: UNVERIFIED: from search snippet. V1 attempt on 2026-11-21: northsaanich.ca returns 301 to www.northsaanich.ca, which is not on this session's allowed hosts, so the page could not be opened. Allow www.northsaanich.ca to verify.

facts.text: In North Saanich a regulated tree is generally one 20 cm or more in diameter at breast height, plus certain protected species at smaller sizes. Staff may inspect and require replacement trees.
facts.sourceTitle: Residential Tree Permit Guide (District of North Saanich)
facts.excerpt: a tree with a D.B.H. of 20 cm or greater
facts.note: UNVERIFIED: from search snippet. The URL redirects (301) to www.northsaanich.ca, which is not on this session's allowed hosts.

facts.text: North Saanich's tree bylaw prohibits topping. If a tree is cut before a permit is issued, the owner must notify the District and file a retroactive application.
facts.sourceTitle: Residential Tree Permit Guide (District of North Saanich)
facts.note: UNVERIFIED: from search snippet, and the excerpt was paraphrased by the search tool. The URL redirects (301) to www.northsaanich.ca, which is not on this session's allowed hosts.

facts.text: North Saanich's Development Permit Areas include Marine Uplands and Foreshore (DPA 1), Sensitive Ecosystems (DPA 3) and Steep Slopes (DPA 4), set out in section 5.10 of the 2025 OCP (Bylaw No. 1587). Waterfront and hillside work can need a DP.
facts.sourceTitle: Development Permits | District of North Saanich
facts.excerpt: 1: Marine Uplands and Foreshore; DPA No. 3: Sensitive Ecosystems; DPA No. 4: Steep Slopes
facts.note: UNVERIFIED: from search snippet. The URL redirects (301) to www.northsaanich.ca, which is not on this session's allowed hosts. The '10 cm in DPAs' claim from research/areas.json is STILL UNVERIFIED and must not be published.

facts.text: Nearly 35% of North Saanich is in the Agricultural Land Reserve, and its OCP aims to keep the community's rural, agricultural and marine character. Acreages and hobby farms are typical lot types.
facts.sourceTitle: Agriculture & Land Security | District of North Saanich
facts.excerpt: nearly 35% of the District is within the Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR)
facts.note: UNVERIFIED: from search snippet. The URL redirects (301) to www.northsaanich.ca, which is not on this session's allowed hosts. 'Acreages and hobby farms are typical' is our framing.

facts.text: North Saanich has provincial groundwater observation wells. In the October 2026 report, a bedrock well there was at the low end of its historical range, which matters to properties on private wells.
facts.sourceTitle: West Coast Groundwater Report (BC River Forecast Centre)
facts.excerpt: a crystalline bedrock well reads at the low end of its historical range
facts.note: UNVERIFIED: from search snippet, and the excerpt was paraphrased by the search tool. bcrfc.env.gov.bc.ca is not on this session's allowed hosts. The report changes over time, so do not quote a reading. prov-private-well-drought (verified) covers the advice.

facts.text: North Saanich runs its own water mains, fed by bulk CRD water through the Saanich Peninsula system, and CRD lawn-watering schedules apply on that supply. Properties on private wells follow provincial well guidance instead.
facts.sourceTitle: Water Conservation | District of North Saanich
facts.excerpt: watering schedules are in effect within the District of North Saanich
facts.note: UNVERIFIED: from search snippet, and the excerpt was paraphrased by the search tool. www.northsaanich.ca is not on this session's allowed hosts. The CRD 'Greater Victoria Drinking Water Supply System' map (crd.ca) labels North Saanich, but its text does not say which parcels are served, so it does not confirm this fact.

facts.text: North Saanich encourages owners to reduce or stop cosmetic pesticide use. Whether it has a residential pesticide bylaw was not confirmed, so check with the District before advising.
facts.sourceTitle: Pesticide Use | District of North Saanich
facts.excerpt: encourages property owners to reduce or eliminate the cosmetic use of pesticides on their properties
facts.note: UNVERIFIED: from search snippet. www.northsaanich.ca is not on this session's allowed hosts. CORRECTED wording: removed 'Search found no residential pesticide bylaw', because a negative search is not evidence.

facts.text: Provincial (BC): owners with private wells are advised to conserve water year-round, including through drought-friendly landscaping. They should also follow local watering restrictions, check nearby observation wells in the same aquifer, and consider collecting rainwater for gardens.
facts.sourceTitle: What to do if your well goes dry (Province of BC brochure)
facts.excerpt: This should be done year-round and can include using less water, using low-water appliances, and drought-friendly landscaping.
facts.note: V1: confirmed on the live PDF (section 'Drought preparation and planning'). Rainwater collection was added from the same section; the brochure notes that rainwater is not safe to drink unless treated.

facts.text: Regional (CRD, not municipal): every year from May 1 to September 30, Stage 1 of the CRD Water Conservation Bylaw applies on the regional water supply. Lawns may be watered two days a week by address (even: Wednesday and Saturday; odd: Thursday and Sunday), 4 to 10 a.m. or 7 to 10 p.m.; automatic systems may start at 12:01 a.m. Trees, shrubs, flowers and vegetables may be sprinkled any day in those hours, and hand watering and drip are allowed any time. A strata complex uses the complex's street address.
facts.sourceTitle: Regional Watering Schedule | Capital Regional District
facts.excerpt: Stage 1 Watering Schedule of the Water Conservation Bylaw No. 4099 for the Regional Water Supply System is in effect May 1 through September 30 every year.
facts.note: V1: confirmed. CORRECTED: the old URL (crd.bc.ca/education/...) is not reachable and www.crd.ca/node/4919 redirects here, so the URL was updated. The old excerpt 'The watering schedule days only apply to lawns!' is not on the current page and was replaced. The bylaw applies to customers of the Regional Water Supply System; properties on private wells are not covered.

facts.text: Regional (CRD): invasive plants can go to Hartland Landfill in bags marked 'Invasive Species' or in covered loads. Knotweed needs a controlled waste permit and must not go to municipal yard-waste drop-offs.
facts.excerpt: Invasive species can be disposed of at Hartland Landfill. They must be in bags marked “Invasive Species” or in covered loads.
facts.note: V1: NEW shared regional fact (same id in every V1 file).
